title: Temp Files & VCS Artifacts
description: Development leftovers and temporary files exposed on production systems.

attacks.name: .swp / .swo
attacks.desc: Exposed Vim swap files can contain source code or unsaved edits from a developer session.
attacks.prevention: Exclude editor swap files from deployments and deny access to hidden temporary-file extensions.

attacks.name: ~ backup files
attacks.desc: Editor backup files with a trailing tilde may reveal earlier source or configuration content.
attacks.prevention: Write backups to private storage outside the document root and block direct HTTP access.

attacks.name: .DS_Store
attacks.desc: A .DS_Store file can disclose filenames from a directory even when listing is disabled.
attacks.prevention: Exclude .DS_Store files from builds and restrict directory metadata at the web server.

attacks.name: Thumbs.db
attacks.desc: Windows thumbnail caches can reveal names or previews of files once present in a folder.
attacks.prevention: Keep Windows thumbnail caches out of published assets and remove them during packaging.

attacks.name: ~$file.docx
attacks.desc: Office lock files may reveal document names or user details when copied to a web root.
attacks.prevention: Exclude Office lock files from deployment and store documents in access-controlled locations.

attacks.name: .svn/entries
attacks.desc: Exposed Subversion metadata can disclose repository structure or source references.

attacks.name: .hg/
attacks.desc: An exposed Mercurial directory can reveal repository history and application source.

attacks.name: .bzr/
attacks.desc: An exposed Bazaar directory can reveal version-control metadata and source files.

attacks.name: composer.lock / package-lock.json
attacks.desc: Lockfiles can reveal exact dependency versions, which aids inventory and patch review.

attacks.name: .idea/ .vscode/
attacks.desc: Public editor configuration folders can reveal project paths, tasks, or environment assumptions.

attacks.name: phpinfo.php
attacks.desc: An exposed phpinfo page can reveal loaded modules, paths, and environment configuration.

attacks.name: /server-status, /server-info
attacks.desc: Apache status or information endpoints can disclose active requests and server configuration.

attacks.name: /.well-known/ enum
attacks.desc: Well-known endpoints should be inventoried because some expose service metadata or configuration.
